title: Fire Guard for Torch Operations
page_numbering: PDF page index (1 = first page of the PDF file)

questions.question: At which of these locations must the fire watch for torch operations be performed by an F-60 fire guard?
questions.explanation: F-60 fire guards are required at construction sites, on any rooftop, and in any building when the operator holds a citywide torch permit.

source.quote: F-60 certificate of fitness fire guards are required to perform the fire watch for torch operations at (a) construction sites, (b) on any rooftop

questions.question: Can an F-60 Certificate of Fitness holder serve as a watchperson at a construction site?
options: Yes, F-60 covers all construction site duties
Yes, if the site is under 50,000 square feet
No; a watchperson must take the S-60 test
questions.explanation: The F-60 is NOT qualified to serve as a construction site watchperson; that requires the S-60.

source.quote: Applicants who apply to be a watchperson should take S-60 Certificate of Fitness test.

questions.question: Can an F-60 Certificate of Fitness holder serve as a fire guard for impairment at a construction site?
options: No; that requires the F-01 Certificate of Fitness
Yes, if no hot work is being done
questions.explanation: The F-60 is NOT qualified to serve as a fire guard for impairment; applicants should take the F-01 test.

source.quote: Applicants who apply to be a fire guard for impairment should take the F-01 Certificate of Fitness test.

questions.question: An FDNY permit is required for hot work storing, using or handling any flammable gas over how much?
questions.explanation: A permit is required for flammable gas (e.g., LPG, CNG or acetylene) over 400 SCF.

source.quote: storing, using, or handling any flammable gas (e.g. LPG or CNG or acetylene) over 400 SCF.

questions.question: An FDNY permit is required for hot work storing, using or handling any oxidizing gas (e.g., oxygen) over how much?
questions.explanation: A permit is required for oxidizing gas over 504 SCF.

source.quote: storing, using, or handling any oxidizing gas (e.g. oxygen) over 504 SCF

questions.question: For LPG, 400 SCF is approximately how many pounds?
questions.explanation: For LPG, 400 SCF is approximately 47 lbs.

source.quote: For LPG, 400 SCF is approximately 47 lbs.

questions.question: What is the maximum weight of any single standard portable LPG container?
questions.explanation: Any single standard portable LPG container must not exceed 100 lbs.

source.quote: Any single standard portable LPG container must not exceed 100 lbs in weight.

questions.question: What is required to use LPG/propane on an occupied roof?
options: A sign posted at the roof door
An affidavit from a licensed Architect or Engineer stating the roof is non-combustible
Verbal permission from the building super
questions.explanation: Use of LPG/propane on an occupied roof requires an affidavit from a licensed professional stating the roof is non-combustible.

source.quote: Use of LPG/Propane on an occupied roof requires an affidavit from a licensed professional (Architect or Engineer) stating the roof is constructed of non-combustible material(s).

questions.question: How long is a permanent site-specific FDNY permit valid?
questions.explanation: Permanent permits are valid for 12 months only; every permit or renewal requires an inspection.

source.quote: Permanent permits are valid for 12 months only.

questions.question: Under a citywide permit, the activity at any individual location may not exceed how long?
questions.explanation: Citywide permit activity at one location may not exceed 30 calendar days; longer requires a site-specific permit.

source.quote: The duration of such activity at any individual location does not exceed 30 calendar days

questions.question: Can an FDNY permit be transferred to a new owner of the business?
options: Yes, if the operation stays the same
No; any change in ownership requires a new permit
questions.explanation: Permits are not transferable; any change in occupancy, operation, tenancy or ownership requires a new permit.

source.quote: All permits are not transferable, and any change in occupancy, operation, tenancy or ownership requires that a new permit be issued.

questions.question: Who issues the hot work program authorization?
options: The responsible person (it is not issued by the FDNY)
questions.explanation: Hot work program authorization is NOT issued by the FDNY; it is signed and issued by the responsible person.

source.quote: Hot work program authorization is NOT issued by the FDNY, it must be signed and issued by the responsible person

questions.question: For how long after the work is complete must the hot work authorization remain available for inspection?
questions.explanation: The authorization must be available during the work and for 48 hours after the work is complete.

source.quote: available for inspection by any representative of the Fire Department during the performance of the work, and for 48 hours after the work is complete.

questions.question: According to the study material, what is the source of ignition in about 60% of all fires in industrial occupancies?
options: Sparks and pieces of hot metal
questions.explanation: Usually it is not the flame but the sparks and pieces of hot metal that cause fires.

source.quote: sparks and pieces of hot metal are the source of ignition in about 60% of all fires in industrial occupancies.

questions.question: Why should clothing with pockets or cuffs be avoided while doing hot work?
options: They block the view of the fire guard
They make it hard to climb ladders
Sparks or slag can catch in cuffs or pockets
They are against the dress code
questions.explanation: Sparks or slag can catch in cuffs or pockets.

source.quote: Avoid clothing with pockets or cuffs while working. Sparks or slag can catch in cuffs or pockets.

questions.question: For hot work under a citywide permit, how far in advance must the premises owner be notified in writing?
questions.explanation: The citywide permit holder must notify the owner in writing at least 48 hours before hot work starts.

source.quote: the owner of the premises of the hot work operation areas must be notified in writing by the citywide permit holder at least 48 hours

questions.question: How often must the responsible person conduct the pre-hot work check?
options: Only on the first day of a project
At least once per day, and before hot work is authorized
questions.explanation: The pre-hot work check must be done by the responsible person at least once per day and before hot work is authorized.

source.quote: The pre-hot work check must be conducted by the responsible person at least once per day and before the hot work is authorized.

questions.question: Hot work involving cutting or welding must be conducted at least how far from combustible materials (unless shielded)?
questions.explanation: The 35-foot rule applies to cutting and welding; other hot work uses 25 feet.

source.quote: Hot work operations involving cutting or welding must be conducted at least 35 feet from combustible materials and combustible waste

questions.question: Hot work OTHER than cutting or welding must be conducted at least how far from combustible materials (unless shielded)?
questions.explanation: All other hot work must be at least 25 feet from combustible materials and waste, or shielded.

source.quote: All other hot work operations must be conducted at least 25 feet from combustible materials and combustible waste

questions.question: When hot work near sprinklers extends over several days, when must the shields over sprinkler heads be removed?
options: Only when the whole project is complete
At the end of each workday
questions.explanation: Damp cloth guards or noncombustible barriers must be removed at the end of each workday if the work extends over several days.

source.quote: If the work extends over several days, the shields must be removed at the end of each workday.

questions.question: Which Certificate of Fitness is required for the person doing torch operations using oxygen and a flammable gas?
questions.explanation: G-60 is required for the torch operator using oxygen and flammable gas; F-60 is for the fire guard.

source.quote: G-60 certificates of fitness are required for torch operations using oxygen and a flammable gas

questions.question: How many torches may one person operate at a time?
options: Two, if they are close together
Any number, if a fire guard is present
Only one, and it must not be left unattended while ignited
questions.explanation: Each person must operate only one torch at a time and never leave it unattended while ignited.

source.quote: Each person must operate only one torch at a time, and the torch must not be left unattended while ignited.

questions.question: When may hot work be performed on a container that has held a flammable liquid?
options: Only with a damp cloth over it
Any time, if it is empty
Only after it has been thoroughly cleaned and purged
questions.explanation: Hot work must not be performed on such a container until it has been thoroughly cleaned and purged.

source.quote: until the container or equipment has been thoroughly cleaned and purged.

questions.question: Is it permitted to perform welding or cutting while supported by or resting on compressed gas containers?
options: Yes, if the containers are empty
Yes, with a fire guard present
questions.explanation: Welding or cutting while supported by or resting on compressed gas containers is prohibited.

source.quote: It is prohibited to perform welding or cutting when supported by or resting on any compressed gas containers.

questions.question: Torch use in a repair garage located on a property with a motor-fuel dispensing facility must be done where?
options: Within a fire-rated enclosure approved by the Building Department
questions.explanation: It must be conducted within a fire-rated enclosure with fireproof, self-closing doors.

source.quote: must be conducted within a fire-rated enclosure (approved by the Building Department).

questions.question: May persons conducting a fire watch for hot work have other duties?
options: Yes, they may also be the site safety manager
Yes, if the hot work is brief
Yes, they may help the torch operator
questions.explanation: Persons conducting a fire watch must keep constant watch and must not have other duties.

source.quote: The persons conducting a fire watch must not have other duties.

questions.question: What is the minimum rating of the portable fire extinguisher required near general hot work?
questions.explanation: At least one extinguisher with a minimum 2-A:20-B:C rating must be readily accessible (3-A:40-B:C for roofing).

source.quote: At least one portable fire extinguisher with a minimum 2-A:20-B:C rating must be provided and readily accessible

questions.question: What minimum extinguisher rating is required for roofing operations using heat-producing systems?
questions.explanation: Roofing operations need at least one multipurpose extinguisher rated at least 3-A:40-B:C.

source.quote: There must be at least one multipurpose portable fire extinguisher with a minimum 3-A 40-B:C rating for roofing

questions.question: Within what distance of the hot work location and fire guard position must the required portable fire extinguisher be readily accessible?
questions.explanation: The required extinguisher must be readily accessible within 30 feet of the hot work and the fire guard's position.

source.quote: must be readily accessible within 30 feet of the location where hot work is performed and where the fire guards are positioned.

questions.question: Is it lawful to install roofing material using a torch on a roof of combustible construction?
options: Yes, if the roof is wet
Yes, with an F-60 fire guard
questions.explanation: It is unlawful to install roofing material with a torch on a roof of combustible construction.

source.quote: It must be unlawful to install any roofing material using a torch on a roof of combustible construction

questions.question: A single fire guard may watch more than one torch operation on the same floor if each operation is no more than how far away (by actual path of travel)?
questions.explanation: One fire guard may cover multiple torch operations on the same level if each is within 50 feet by path of travel and in view.

source.quote: if each torch operation is not more than 50 feet from the fire guard, as measured by the actual path of travel

questions.question: During torch operations on the roof of a building, how must fire guards be on duty?
options: Only at the start of the work
On continuous duty during all torch operations
questions.explanation: Fire guards must be on continuous duty during all torch operations on a roof.

source.quote: Fire guards must be on continuous duty during all torch operations on the roof of a building.

questions.question: When is an additional F-60 fire guard required on the floor below a torch operation?
options: Only if the floor below is occupied by tenants
When the torch operation is at or near the edge of an unenclosed floor or near a floor opening
questions.explanation: An additional F-60 fire guard is required below when sparks and slag may travel to lower floors, such as at an unenclosed edge or floor opening.

source.quote: Additional F-60 fire guard is required to perform fire watch on floor below if the torch operation is being conducted at or near the edge

questions.question: If sparks or slag are observed to extend beyond 35 feet and may expose lower floors, what must happen?
options: Move the fire guard to the roof
The torch operation must be immediately discontinued and the floors below inspected
questions.explanation: The operation must stop immediately and the floors below must be inspected for any fire condition.

source.quote: the torch operation must be immediately discontinued, and the floors or levels below must be inspected for any fire condition.

questions.question: How long must the fire watch continue after hot work ends?
questions.explanation: The fire watch must continue for a minimum of 30 minutes after hot work ends; it may be extended.

source.quote: The fire watch must continue for a minimum of 30 minutes after the hot work ends.

questions.question: For a CNG or LPG torch operation, when are the two post-work inspections conducted?
questions.explanation: First inspection 30 minutes after completion; second inspection 1 hour after completion, to catch smoldering fires.

source.quote: the first inspection must be conducted 30 minutes after completion of torch operations; the second inspection 1 hour after completion

questions.question: Who receives and retains the fire guard's signed inspection report?
options: The person in charge of the torch operations
questions.explanation: The report must be submitted to and retained by the person in charge of the torch operations.

source.quote: This report must be submitted to and retained by the person in charge of the torch operations.

questions.question: Oxygen containers, valves, regulators and hoses must be kept free of what?
questions.explanation: Oxygen equipment must be kept free of oil or grease and not handled with oily hands, gloves or tools.

source.quote: Oxygen containers and oxygen container valves, regulators, hose, and other apparatus and fittings must be kept free of oil or grease.

questions.question: When must the torch valve be closed and the gas supply to the torch completely shut off?
options: When hot work is discontinued for 1 hour or more
Only at the end of the week
Only when the cylinder is empty
questions.explanation: The torch valve must be closed and gas shut off when hot work stops for 1 hour or more.

source.quote: the gas supply to the torch completely shut off when hot work operations are discontinued for a period of 1 hour or more.

questions.question: How must piping equipment or systems be tested for suspected leaks?
questions.explanation: It is unlawful to test for leaks using a flame; soapy water must be used.

source.quote: Tests for suspected leaks in piping equipment and systems must be done using soapy water.

questions.question: From which direction should a fire be approached?
questions.explanation: Approach the flame from upwind to avoid being burned; never approach from downwind.

source.quote: The flame must be approached from an upwind direction.

questions.question: Where should the dry chemical stream be directed when extinguishing a gas fire?
options: Toward the point where the flame begins
At the top of the flame
At the center of the flame
questions.explanation: Direct the stream toward the point where the flame begins, not at the center of the flame.

source.quote: The dry chemical stream must be directed toward the point where the flame begins.

questions.question: A gas cylinder fire cannot be shut off because the fire is near the shut-off valve. What should you do?
options: Extinguish the flame immediately with an extinguisher
Spray water directly on the valve
Pick up the cylinder and move it
Allow the flame to burn itself out, call 911, and prevent spread to surroundings
questions.explanation: When the gas cannot be shut off and supply is limited, let the flame burn itself out and call 911; never extinguish the flame unless the gas supply is off.

source.quote: allow the flame to burn itself out and call 911.

questions.question: Which fires must be reported, according to the Fire Guard Daily Log for Hot Work?
options: Only fires larger than 10 square feet
Fires of all sizes, even if immediately extinguished
Only fires that need the FDNY
questions.explanation: Fires of all sizes must be reported even if they are immediately extinguished.

source.quote: Fires of all sizes must be reported, even if they are immediately extinguished.

questions.question: If a fire alarm system is taken off-line during hot work to avoid unwarranted alarms, what must be provided?
questions.explanation: Fire watch for impairment must be provided when the alarm system is off-line.

source.quote: Fire watch for impairment must be provided when the alarm system is off-line.

questions.question: When must visible hazard identification signs be posted at a hot work area?
options: Where the hot work area is accessible to persons other than the operator
questions.explanation: Signs must be posted conspicuously where others besides the operator can access the hot work area.

source.quote: Where the hot work area is accessible to persons other than the operator of the hot work equipment, visible hazard identification signs must be posted

questions.question: What should the fire guard know about lithium-ion battery fires and fire extinguishers?
options: Fire extinguishers do not work on lithium-ion battery fires
Any ABC extinguisher will put them out
questions.explanation: The study material states fire extinguishers do not work on lithium-ion battery fires, and reignition is common.

source.quote: Fire Extinguishers do not work on lithium-ion batteries fires.
